steps.body: Next come 4, 5, and 6. New shapes, same promise: each mark names its own amount, one more than the mark before.
steps.narration: Next come 4, 5, and 6. New shapes, same promise: each mark names its own amount, one more than the mark before.

widget.prompt: Build the amount the numeral 5 promises.

commonCounts.feedback: Four leaves one square of the row empty; the mark 5 asks for the full row.
Six spills past the row; the mark 5 stops at five.

widget.missFeedback: The numeral fixes the count: exactly five, no more, no fewer.
widget.successFeedback: Five — a full row of the frame, and the mark 5 names exactly it.

predict.prompt: Which mark can 6 be mistaken for, turned upside-down?
predict.reveal: 6 and 9 are one shape in two orientations — which way the loop sits decides. 0 tempts because it shares the loop, but 0 has no tail — flip 6 any way you like and its tail stays.

cml.actionGoal: Link the written numeral to the exact amount it names for kcw write 456.
invariants: A numeral is a written promise about an amount: it records the last word of a careful count, position gives each digit its job, and the promise survives any change of objects or arrangement — the anchor for kcw write 456.
misconceptions: Treating numerals as decorations, reading digit pairs without position, or matching a numeral to roughly rather than exactly its amount.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more thing joined the group, which single mark of the numeral would have to change?

widget.prompt: 6 and 9 look like the same shape turned around. What tells them apart?

options.label: Which way up the loop sits
options.feedback: Correct — 6 carries its loop at the bottom, 9 at the top; orientation IS the difference.

options.label: Their colour
options.feedback: Numerals have no fixed colour; only the shape and its orientation distinguish them.

options.label: Their size on the page
options.feedback: A big 6 is still 6; size never separates numerals.

options.label: Nothing — they are the same
options.feedback: They name different amounts three apart; the turned loop is the whole signal.

widget.prompt: A group shows 6 dots. Which numeral names that amount?

options.feedback: Correct — the numeral 6 is the written name for a group of exactly 6.
7 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 6.
5 promises fewer dots than the group holds; the count reaches 6.
8 promises more dots than the group holds; the count stops at 6.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 6? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 6 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 7.
8 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 6 lands on 7.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 6: you land on 7.
widget.successFeedback: 7 — the next numeral in the writing order is the next number in the song.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 7.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 6 means one hop, stopping on 7.
